book.notes: Spine order: wrap0000 (cover), h-0 (Gutenberg header, title page, preface, and chapter 1), h-1 onward (several chapters per document). Chapters are split at the TOC anchors, so each href carries a fragment and check_gold.py cuts the document from that anchor to the next TOC anchor. Several TOC labels start with an illustration caption ('He rode a black horse. CHAPTER III.'), and the chapter text starts with that caption. This key covers run chapters 1-12 only, so it sets partial. Entity types follow Annalist's vocabulary (character, place, organization, artifact, event, concept). The text uses U+2019 apostrophes and curly double quotes; compare names with them folded.

ambiguities: Miss Bennet: by etiquette the eldest daughter's title. The key lets Jane's page carry it and fails it on any other sister's page. Elizabeth may carry Miss Eliza Bennet and Miss Elizabeth Bennet.
Eliza: Miss Bingley and Charlotte call Elizabeth Eliza; it is an alias of Elizabeth, not a separate person.
Kitty and Catherine: ch 2 says Kitty, the narration says Catherine from ch 3; the text never states they are one girl, but a reader infers it from the five daughters. Accept either as the page name.
Mr. Hurst's forename and Darcy's forename are not given in ch 1-12.
Miss Darcy is only Miss Darcy or 'your sister' in ch 1-12; Georgiana is not required.

Darcy and Derbyshire: ch 3 gives him a 'large estate in Derbyshire'; the estate is named Pemberley only from ch 6. Owning Derbyshire is marked lenient: a located_in relation from Pemberley also satisfies a reader.
The militia regiment is mostly 'the officers' or 'the regiment'; Colonel Forster's membership is inferred from his rank and the setting, so it is lenient.
Mr. Jones is called in as apothecary; physician_of is lenient for any treats or attends wording.
